title: Understanding the Median Salary Australia 2025 and How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual salary using a 38-hour week. Explore the median salary Australia 2025, tax, super, and award rates with our guide.
salarySummary: For a full-time worker on a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with super paid on top at 12%.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a standard full‑time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. Super is paid on top of this amount at 12% (up to the maximum contribution base).

faqs.q: What is the difference between the median salary and the average salary in Australia?
faqs.a: The median salary is the middle value when all salaries are sorted – half earn more, half earn less. The average (mean) is the total wages divided by the number of workers. Because high earners pull the average up, the median is usually lower. The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes average weekly earnings, but the median salary Australia 2025 is not provided in our reference tables. For a more precise median, check the ABS’s Employee Earnings and Hours release.

faqs.q: Does the calculator on this site include tax and super?
faqs.a: Yes, the timesheet calculator estimates annual pay, tax (using the 2026–27 resident rates and Medicare levy), and super at 12% on top of ordinary earnings. It assumes a 38‑hour week, no overtime, no penalty rates, and no salary sacrifice. The result is an estimate only – your actual pay and tax may differ.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly Rate and Annual Salary

If you’re paid by the hour or considering a salary offer, the first step is to convert your hourly rate into an annual figure. The standard formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For a full‑time employee working 38 hours a week (the typical full‑time week under the Fair Work Act), that becomes:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, at $30 per hour: $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year. Your fortnightly pay (before tax and super) would be $30 × 38 × 2 = $2,280.

This calculation assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It’s a starting point for comparing job offers or understanding your total remuneration.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

Australia’s National Minimum Wage (NMW) is set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, the NMW is **$26.44 per hour**, or **$1,004.90 per week** for a 38‑hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top, making the casual minimum **$33.05 per hour**.

However, most industries have **award rates** that are higher than the NMW. Awards cover specific occupations and set minimum pay, penalties, and allowances. You can check your award using the [pay guides](/blog) on this site. Always compare your rate to the relevant award – not just the national minimum.

Superannuation (super) is paid **on top** of your base salary or hourly rate. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. So if you earn $59,280, your employer must contribute an extra $7,113.60 to your super fund.

## Median Salary Australia 2025: What the Data Shows

The keyword **median salary Australia 2025** often appears in salary discussions, but our reference tables do not include a precise median figure for 2025. Instead, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes **Average Weekly Earnings (AWE)**. For May 2026, full‑time adult ordinary time earnings averaged **$2,083.70 per week** (about $108,352 annually). All employees (including part‑time) averaged **$1,579.20 per week**.

It’s important to understand that an **average** is not the same as a **median**. The median is the middle point – half of all workers earn less, half earn more. Because high incomes pull the average upward, the median is typically lower. For a more accurate picture of typical pay, look for the ABS’s Employee Earnings and Hours release, which provides median figures by occupation and industry.

In the meantime, you can use our [reference tables](/data) to see average pay for various groups, but remember these are averages, not medians. If you’re researching a specific job, check industry‑specific sources or the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) topic on this site.

## Converting Hourly to Annual: A Step‑by‑Step Example

Let’s walk through an example using a rate of $35 per hour.

1. **Weekly pay**: $35 × 38 hours = $1,330
2. **Fortnightly pay**: $1,330 × 2 = $2,660
3. **Annual gross**: $1,330 × 52 = $69,160

Now estimate tax and super. Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Tax‑free threshold: $0 – $18,200
- 15% on $18,201 – $45,000
- 30% on $45,001 – $135,000
- 37% on $135,001 – $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

For $69,160:
- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on next $26,800 ($18,201–$45,000): $26,800 × 15% = $4,020
- Tax on remaining $24,160 ($45,001–$69,160): $24,160 × 30% = $7,248
- Total tax: $11,268
- Medicare levy (2% of taxable income): $1,383.20
- Total tax + Medicare: $12,651.20
- Net annual pay: $69,160 – $12,651.20 = $56,508.80

Super is paid on top: $69,160 × 12% = $8,299.20 (up to the contribution cap).

Note: This estimate uses the 2025–26 Medicare reduction thresholds for singles (not confirmed for 2026–27), so your actual Medicare may differ. No HELP, surcharge, or salary packaging is deducted.

## Tax and Super Considerations

Your employer must pay super on your ordinary earnings, but it’s not deducted from your salary – it’s an additional cost to them. The super guarantee rate is 12% from 1 July 2026, and it applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. If your annual salary exceeds that, super is capped.

Tax is calculated on your gross income after any salary sacrifice arrangements (which are not included in this estimate). The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income, but may be reduced if you’re on a low income. The 2026–27 budget may change thresholds, so always check the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) for the latest.

## Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) (home page) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading with a checkbox. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the calculator adds it for you. It then shows your weekly, fortnightly, and annual pay, plus estimated tax and super.

For award‑specific rates, visit the [pay guides](/blog) to find the correct minimum for your job. You can also explore topics like [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) and [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home) for more details.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
